```bash
@test "actionlint passes on release.yml" {
    command -v actionlint > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "actionlint is not installed (brew install actionlint)"
    cd "$ROOT"
    run actionlint "$WORKFLOWS/release.yml"
    if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}
```

Bats runs with `LANG=C`, so the prelude reads the workflow as UTF-8 explicitly: the workflow's comments hold non-ASCII text, and Ruby would otherwise raise `invalid byte sequence in US-ASCII` from the first check that scans the raw text.

- [ ] **Step 6: Run them to verify they fail**

Run: `bats scripts/tests/workflows.bats`
Expected: FAIL. `1..25`. Tests 1 to 23 are `not ok` with `release.yml is missing`. `ok 24 no workflow uses pull_request_target` (today's `ci.yml` has no such trigger). Test 25 is `ok … # skip actionlint is not installed` without `actionlint`, and `not ok` with it, because the file does not exist yet.

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the workflow** — `.github/workflows/release.yml`

The action lines carry majors (`@v7 # v7`), because the commit SHAs are looked up in Step 9. Every value a run block uses is an environment variable, so the file has no `${{ }}` inside `run:`.

```yaml
name: Release

# One pushed tag vX.Y.Z runs `build` (the signing secrets, behind the `release`
# environment's approval), then `publish` (no secrets), `pages` and `fixture`.
# A manual run with a version is a dry run: `build` only, and nothing is
# created on GitHub (Plan 6, Ruling 13). Run blocks stay thin: they call
# scripts/, which bats tests. workflows.bats pins this file's shape.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "X.Y.Z to rehearse; nothing is published"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build, sign and package
    runs-on: xcode-27
    timeout-minutes: 90
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # $GITHUB_ENV does not cross jobs, so the later jobs read these outputs.
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.version }}
      build_number: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.build_number }}
      strict: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.strict_release }}
      fixture: ${{ steps.fixture.outputs.written }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7 # v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          # A shallow checkout leaves vendor/mole without its tags, and the
          # preflight needs the default branch and every tag.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # release-preflight.sh prints KEY=VALUE lines (TAG, VERSION, BUILD_NUMBER,
      # ARCHIVE_NAME, SOURCE_NAME, STRICT_RELEASE, DRY_RUN, APP). They go to
      # $GITHUB_ENV for this job's steps, and, lower-cased, to the step outputs.
      - name: Preflight
        id: preflight
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          INPUT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PUBLISHED_TAGS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/published-tags.txt
        run: |
          gh release list --exclude-drafts --limit 1000 --json tagName --jq '.[].tagName' > "$PUBLISHED_TAGS_FILE"
          VISIBILITY="$(gh repo view --json visibility --jq .visibility)"
          export VISIBILITY
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = workflow_dispatch ]; then
              preflight=(scripts/release-preflight.sh --dry-run "$INPUT_VERSION")
          else
              preflight=(scripts/release-preflight.sh "$GITHUB_REF_NAME")
          fi
          if ! "${preflight[@]}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/preflight.env"; then
              cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/preflight.env"
              exit 1
          fi
          grep -E '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=' "$RUNNER_TEMP/preflight.env" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          awk -F= '{ key = tolower($1); sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print key "=" $0 }' "$RUNNER_TEMP/preflight.env" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # No cache: this job holds the signing secrets, so it restores nothing
      # that another workflow could have written.
      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7 # v7
        with:
          go-version-file: vendor/mole/go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Install tools
        run: brew install xcodegen bats-core

      - name: Show the toolchain
        run: |
          sw_vers
          xcodebuild -version
          xcodegen --version
          go version
          bats --version
          python3 --version
          gh --version

      # KEYCHAIN and SIGNING_SHA1 go to $GITHUB_ENV. The keychain is removed
      # again right after the build, whatever happens.
      - name: Import the signing identity
        env:
          RFM_SIGNING_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.RFM_SIGNING_P12_BASE64 }}
          RFM_SIGNING_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.RFM_SIGNING_P12_PASSWORD }}
        run: scripts/import-signing-identity.sh create "$RUNNER_TEMP/rfm-signing.keychain-db" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Plan 5's per-release hook (scripts/release-hooks/token-fixture). Until it
      # exists the dispatcher skips it with a notice, both variables are empty,
      # and nothing is written. No flag makes it mandatory yet (Ruling 12).
      # When the hook lists files, they travel to the fixture job as one tar.
      # COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 and --no-xattrs keep macOS tar from adding AppleDouble
      # ._<name> entries, which the fixture job would commit (Task 11's finding).
      - name: Token fixture (release hook)
        id: fixture
        env:
          RFM_FIXTURE_TOKEN_URL: ${{ vars.RFM_FIXTURE_TOKEN_URL }}
          RFM_FIXTURE_TOKEN_KEY: ${{ secrets.RFM_FIXTURE_TOKEN_KEY }}
        run: |
          paths="$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-paths.txt"
          scripts/release-hook.sh token-fixture "$VERSION" "$RUNNER_TEMP/published-tags.txt" "$paths"
          if [ -s "$paths" ]; then
              COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar --no-xattrs -cf "$RUNNER_TEMP/token-fixture.tar" -T "$paths"
              echo "written=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
              echo "written=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Build the patched engine
        run: scripts/ensure-engine.sh

      - name: Generate the Xcode project
        run: xcodegen generate

      # RFM_NO_ENGINE_BUILD=1: the "Prepare engine" phase fails instead of
      # rebuilding, so the app embeds the engine built above. Command-line
      # settings override Config/Signing.xcconfig.
      - name: Universal Release build
        env:
          RFM_NO_ENGINE_BUILD: "1"
        run: >-
          xcodebuild -project RoomForMac.xcodeproj -scheme RoomForMac
          -configuration Release -destination "generic/platform=macOS"
          -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData
          MARKETING_VERSION="$VERSION" CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$BUILD_NUMBER"
          CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="RoomForMac Self-Signed"
          OTHER_CODE_SIGN_FLAGS="--keychain $KEYCHAIN"
          build

      # Nothing after the build signs anything, so the keychain goes now.
      - name: Remove the signing keychain
        if: always()
        run: scripts/import-signing-identity.sh delete "$RUNNER_TEMP/rfm-signing.keychain-db"

      # RFM_ALLOW_PROMPTS=1 also checks the bundled `status-go --json`, as in ci.yml.
      - name: Check the app
        env:
          RFM_ALLOW_PROMPTS: "1"
        run: |
          scripts/check-release-app.sh "$APP" --version "$VERSION"
          APP="$APP" EXPECT_UNIVERSAL=1 EXPECT_HARDENED=1 bats scripts/tests/app_bundle.bats

      - name: Make the disk image
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/release
          scripts/make-dmg.sh "$APP" build/release/RoomForMac.dmg

      # A dry run has no tag, and make-source-archive.sh archives a tag: it gets
      # a local, throwaway one that is never pushed.
      - name: Make the update and source archives
        run: |
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ] && ! git rev-parse --quiet --verify "refs/tags/$TAG" > /dev/null; then
              git tag "$TAG"
          fi
          scripts/make-update-archive.sh "$APP" "build/release/$ARCHIVE_NAME"
          scripts/make-source-archive.sh "$TAG" "build/release/$SOURCE_NAME"

      # The appcast keeps every earlier item, so the previous one must be found
      # whenever a release exists: a failed download stops the job here instead
      # of building a feed that forgets old versions. Only a repository with no
      # published release starts from nothing. make-appcast.sh then checks that
      # every old item survives byte for byte.
      - name: Generate the appcast
        env:
          SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          notes="release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ] && [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
              notes=release-notes/TEMPLATE.md
          fi
          args=(--archive "build/release/$ARCHIVE_NAME" --notes "$notes" --tag "$TAG" --out build/release/appcast.xml)
          if [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/published-tags.txt" ]; then
              gh release download --pattern appcast.xml --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/previous"
              args+=(--previous "$RUNNER_TEMP/previous/appcast.xml")
          fi
          scripts/make-appcast.sh "${args[@]}"

      # latest.json and SHA256SUMS, then a check that the folder holds exactly
      # the six release files and that they agree with one another.
      - name: Write the release summary
        run: |
          scripts/release-summary.sh --dmg build/release/RoomForMac.dmg --tag "$TAG" > build/release/latest.json
          (cd build/release && shasum -a 256 RoomForMac.dmg "$ARCHIVE_NAME" "$SOURCE_NAME" > SHA256SUMS)
          scripts/release-publish.sh check-files build/release "$VERSION"

      - name: Upload the release files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7 # v7
        with:
          name: release-files
          path: build/release/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 7 || 30 }}

      - name: Upload the token fixture
        if: steps.fixture.outputs.written == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7 # v7
        with:
          name: token-fixture
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/token-fixture.tar
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 7 || 90 }}

  # No secrets and no checkout credentials here: the job that can write
  # releases never sees a signing key. The draft is published only once all six
  # files are attached, so releases/latest/download/* never points at a release
  # without them.
  publish:
    name: Publish the GitHub release
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.build.outputs.tag }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build.outputs.build_number }}
    steps:
      # The release notes, the scripts and the feed URL come from the tagged commit.
      - name: Check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7 # v7
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            Config
            release-notes
            scripts
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download the release files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8 # v8
        with:
          name: release-files
          path: release-files

      - name: Verify the release files
        run: scripts/release-publish.sh check-files release-files "$VERSION"

      # A draft left by an earlier failed run is deleted. A published release
      # for the tag fails the job, and nothing is touched.
      - name: Replace a leftover draft
        run: scripts/release-publish.sh replace-draft "$TAG"

      - name: Create the draft release
        run: >-
          gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --draft
          --title "RoomForMac $VERSION" --notes-file "release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          release-files/RoomForMac.dmg
          "release-files/RoomForMac-$VERSION.tar.xz"
          "release-files/RoomForMac-$VERSION-source.tar.gz"
          release-files/appcast.xml
          release-files/latest.json
          release-files/SHA256SUMS

      - name: Publish as latest
        run: gh release edit "$TAG" --draft=false --latest

      # Up to five minutes: the feed URL answers through releases/latest/download.
      - name: Check the live feed
        run: scripts/release-publish.sh check-feed "$BUILD_NUMBER"

  # Every Pages deployment replaces the whole site, so this job stages all of
  # it. The feed is a release asset, never part of the site (Ruling 3).
  # The needs context holds direct dependencies only: `build` is listed for its
  # strict output.
  pages:
    name: Deploy the site
    needs: [build, publish]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    concurrency:
      group: pages
      cancel-in-progress: false
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download the release files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8 # v8
        with:
          name: release-files
          path: release-files

      # From 1.0.0 on, --strict refuses [OWNER: …] placeholders (Ruling 12).
      - name: Stage the site
        env:
          STRICT: ${{ needs.build.outputs.strict }}
        run: |
          args=(build/site release-files/latest.json)
          if [ "$STRICT" = 1 ]; then
              args+=(--strict)
          fi
          scripts/stage-site.sh "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload the Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5 # v5
        with:
          path: build/site

      - name: Deploy
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5 # v5

  # Runs only when the token-fixture hook wrote files, so never before Plan 5.
  # It needs the repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve
  # pull requests". The default checkout credentials stay: this job pushes.
  fixture:
    name: Open the token-fixture pull request
    needs: [build, publish]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && needs.build.outputs.fixture == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out the default branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v7 # v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}

      - name: Download the token fixture
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8 # v8
        with:
          name: token-fixture
          path: token-fixture

      - name: Commit and open the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          branch="release/token-fixture-$VERSION"
          tar -tf token-fixture/token-fixture.tar > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-paths.txt"
          if grep -Eq '(^/|(^|/)\.\.(/|$)|^\.github/)' "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-paths.txt"; then
              echo "::error::the fixture lists a path outside the working tree or under .github"
              exit 1
          fi
          tar -xf token-fixture/token-fixture.tar
          git switch --create "$branch"
          git add --pathspec-from-file="$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-paths.txt"
          git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
              commit --message "test(licensing): add the $VERSION token fixture"
          git push origin "$branch"
          gh pr create --base "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" --head "$branch" \
              --title "test(licensing): add the $VERSION token fixture" \
              --body "The token fixture that the $VERSION release fetched from the live server (spec 7.5.4). Merge it before the next release: the hook refuses to build until every published release has its fixture."
```

**Only if Task 4's report says Ruling 5's fallback applies** (the Release build then has no hardened runtime and no entitlements, and Task 9 made `RFM_EXPECT_HARDENED=0` the gate's default). Otherwise skip this paragraph. Two edits, made before Step 8:
- in `release.yml`, step `Check the app`, replace `APP="$APP" EXPECT_UNIVERSAL=1 EXPECT_HARDENED=1 bats scripts/tests/app_bundle.bats` with `APP="$APP" EXPECT_UNIVERSAL=1 bats scripts/tests/app_bundle.bats` (the four hardened-runtime checks then skip, and `check-release-app.sh` checks the fallback through its default);
- in `workflows.bats`, replace `check(run.include?('APP="$APP" EXPECT_UNIVERSAL=1 EXPECT_HARDENED=1 bats scripts/tests/app_bundle.bats'), "app_bundle.bats must run universal and hardened")` with `check(run.include?('APP="$APP" EXPECT_UNIVERSAL=1 bats scripts/tests/app_bundle.bats') && !run.include?('EXPECT_HARDENED=1'), "app_bundle.bats must run universal, without the hardened checks (Ruling 5's fallback)")`.

The Interfaces block's `Check the app` line is read the same way. Every other step is unchanged.

- [ ] **Step 8: Run the checks: only the pin check fails**

Run: `bats scripts/tests/workflows.bats`
Expected: FAIL in exactly one test, `not ok 7 every action is pinned by full commit SHA with a version comment`, followed by twelve lines of the form `release.yml: not pinned as owner/repo@<40 hex> # vN.N.N: uses: actions/checkout@v7 # v7`. The other 24 tests are `ok` (the last is `# skip` without `actionlint`). Test 8 already passes, because it reads the major from the comment.

- [ ] **Step 9: Pin the actions by commit SHA**

Each line `uses: owner/repo@vN # vN` becomes `uses: owner/repo@<commit SHA> # vN.N.N`, with the newest stable release of that major (`sort -V` over the repository's tags; the pattern leaves prereleases out). The loop also reads the action's `runs.using` at that commit and stops unless it is `node24` (or `composite`, as `upload-pages-artifact` is): Node 20 majors no longer run. It needs `gh` signed in; the calls read public data only.

Run:
```bash
bash -euo pipefail << 'EOF'
tmp="$(mktemp)"
for pair in actions/checkout:v7 actions/setup-go:v7 actions/upload-artifact:v7 \
    actions/download-artifact:v8 actions/upload-pages-artifact:v5 actions/deploy-pages:v5; do
    repo="${pair%:*}"
    major="${pair#*:}"
    tag="$(gh api "repos/$repo/tags" --paginate --jq '.[].name' | grep -E "^${major}\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\$" | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
    sha="$(gh api "repos/$repo/commits/$tag" --jq .sha)"
    runtime="$(gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json' "repos/$repo/contents/action.yml?ref=$sha" |
        sed -n 's/^ *using: *//p' | tr -d "'\"")"
    case "$runtime" in
        node24 | composite) ;;
        *)
            echo "error: $repo $tag runs on $runtime, not Node 24" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
    printf '%s %s %s (%s)\n' "$repo" "$sha" "$tag" "$runtime"
    sed "s|uses: $repo@$major # $major\$|uses: $repo@$sha # $tag|" .github/workflows/release.yml > "$tmp"
    cp "$tmp" .github/workflows/release.yml
done
rm -f "$tmp"
EOF
grep -c 'uses: .*@[0-9a-f]\{40\} # v[0-9]*\.[0-9]*\.[0-9]*$' .github/workflows/release.yml
bats scripts/tests/workflows.bats
```

Expected:
- six lines, one per action, each `<owner/repo> <40 hex digits> vN.N.N (node24)`, with `(composite)` for `actions/upload-pages-artifact`. They are the newest tags of majors 7, 7, 7, 8, 5 and 5, in the order checkout, setup-go, upload-artifact, download-artifact, upload-pages-artifact, deploy-pages;
- `12` from `grep -c`: checkout four times, upload-artifact twice, download-artifact three times, and setup-go, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages once each;
- `1..25` and every test `ok` (test 25 is `# skip` without `actionlint`).

If the loop stops with `not Node 24`, the major that the skeleton names no longer runs on Node 24: take the next major, and change it in the `NODE24` table of `workflows.bats` too. Copy the six lines into the As built note. Task 14's `pages.yml` copies the `checkout`, `upload-pages-artifact` and `deploy-pages` pins from this file. A rerun is safe: a line that is already pinned no longer matches the pattern, so the loop leaves it alone.

- [ ] **Step 10: Lint the workflow** — `.github/actionlint.yaml`

```yaml
# actionlint reads this file by itself. xcode-27 is the GitHub-hosted runner
# label for macOS 27 with Xcode 27 (Plan 2, Ruling 14). Some actionlint
# releases do not know it yet and would report `label "xcode-27" is unknown`.
self-hosted-runner:
  labels:
    - xcode-27
```

Run, where `actionlint` is installed (`brew install actionlint`; Task 16 adds it to the Brewfile):
```bash
ruby -ryaml -e 'YAML.load_file(".github/actionlint.yaml"); YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/release.yml")' && echo parsed
actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml
```
Expected: `parsed`, and no output from `actionlint` (exit 0). `actionlint` also runs `shellcheck` on every `run:` block, and `workflows.bats` runs it as its last test.

Without `actionlint`, run what it does to the run blocks (no `${{ }}` reaches a run block, so nothing needs replacing):
```bash
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
ruby -ryaml -e '
YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/release.yml")["jobs"].each do |id, job|
  job["steps"].each_with_index do |step, i|
    next unless step["run"]
    File.write(File.join(ARGV[0], "#{id}-#{i}.sh"), "#!/bin/bash\n" + step["run"] + "\n")
  end
end' "$tmp"
ls "$tmp" | wc -l
shellcheck -s bash -e SC1091,SC2194,SC2050,SC2154,SC2157,SC2043 "$tmp"/*.sh
rm -rf "$tmp"
```
Expected: `21` (the run blocks of the four jobs) and no output from `shellcheck`. The exclusions are the ones `actionlint` passes to `shellcheck` itself. Record which of the two was run.

- [ ] **Step 11: Prove that the checks can fail**

Each edit below breaks the workflow in one way and runs only the check that must catch it (`bats --filter`), against a copy under `$TMPDIR` through `RFM_WORKFLOWS_DIR`. The real files stay untouched. It covers every group of checks: pins, Node 24, keychain, secrets, hook, event guards, environments, triggers, run-block hygiene, `needs`, the publish steps, step order, permissions, checkout credentials, the appcast, the dry-run tag and the build settings.

Run:
```bash
python3 - << 'PY'
import os, re, shutil, subprocess, tempfile

workflows = ".github/workflows"
original = open(os.path.join(workflows, "release.yml")).read()


def replace(old, new):
    def apply(text):
        assert old in text, "the workflow no longer contains: " + old
        return text.replace(old, new, 1)
    return apply


def regex(pattern, new):
    def apply(text):
        out, count = re.subn(pattern, new, text, count=1)
        assert count, "the workflow no longer matches: " + pattern
        return out
    return apply


# (what is broken, the edit, a fragment of the test that must fail)
BREAKS = [
    ("an action pinned to a moving major", regex(r"actions/checkout@[0-9a-f]{40} # v\d+\.\d+\.\d+", "actions/checkout@v7 # v7"), "pinned by full commit SHA"),
    ("an action on a Node 20 major", regex(r"(actions/setup-go@[0-9a-f]{40}) # v\d+\.\d+\.\d+", r"\1 # v5.0.2"), "Node 24"),
    ("the keychain removal without always()", replace("        if: always()\n", ""), "keychain is removed"),
    ("the keychain removal deleting another path", replace('delete "$RUNNER_TEMP/rfm-signing.keychain-db"', 'delete "$RUNNER_TEMP/other.keychain-db"'), "keychain is removed"),
    ("a secret in the publish job", replace("      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build.outputs.build_number }}\n", "      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build.outputs.build_number }}\n      LEAK: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY }}\n"), "secrets are read only by build"),
    ("a signing secret in the wrong build step", replace("      - name: Build the patched engine\n", "      - name: Build the patched engine\n        env:\n          RFM_SIGNING_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.RFM_SIGNING_P12_PASSWORD }}\n"), "secrets are read only by build"),
    ("the hook run as required", replace("scripts/release-hook.sh token-fixture", "scripts/release-hook.sh --required token-fixture"), "release hook is called once"),
    ("a fixture tar with AppleDouble entries", replace("COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar --no-xattrs -cf", "tar -cf"), "release hook is called once"),
    ("the fixture job on a dry run", replace("if: github.event_name == 'push' && needs.build.outputs.fixture == 'true'", "if: needs.build.outputs.fixture == 'true'"), "publish and fixture run only"),
    ("the release environment on publish", replace("    needs: build\n    if: github.event_name == 'push'\n", "    needs: build\n    environment: release\n    if: github.event_name == 'push'\n"), "only build names the release environment"),
    ("a loose tag pattern", replace('"v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"', '"v*"'), "strict tag pattern"),
    ("an expression inside a run block", replace('run: gh release edit "$TAG" --draft=false --latest', 'run: gh release edit "${{ needs.build.outputs.tag }}" --draft=false --latest'), "no run block interpolates"),
    ("pages without build in needs", replace("    needs: [build, publish]\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 15\n    permissions:\n      contents: read\n      pages: write", "    needs: publish\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 15\n    permissions:\n      contents: read\n      pages: write"), "reads needs"),
    ("the draft marked latest at creation", replace('gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --draft', 'gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --draft --latest'), "publish makes a draft"),
    ("an asset dropped from the release", replace("          release-files/SHA256SUMS\n", ""), "publish makes a draft"),
    ("a step renamed", replace("      - name: Deploy\n", "      - name: Ship\n"), "planned order"),
    ("write access for build", replace("    permissions:\n      contents: read\n    # $GITHUB_ENV", "    permissions:\n      contents: write\n    # $GITHUB_ENV"), "four jobs"),
    ("a pull_request_target trigger", replace("  workflow_dispatch:\n", "  pull_request_target:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n"), "pull_request_target"),
    ("a publish checkout that keeps credentials", replace("            scripts\n          persist-credentials: false\n", "            scripts\n"), "checkouts drop their credentials"),
    ("a download error swallowed", replace('--dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/previous"', '--dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/previous" || true'), "appcast step fails closed"),
```

**Decisions this task takes inside those requirements** (each is one edit to change):
- **Where the site's links point.** Pages other than `404.html` use relative links (`assets/site.css`, `../privacy/`), because the site is served under `/RoomForMac/` now and possibly at the root of a domain later. `stage-site.sh` refuses a link that starts with `/`, since it would break under the project path. `404.html` is served at any depth, so it uses `@RFM_SITE_URL@` links, which the link check maps back to files.
- **The link check.** `stage-site.sh` follows every `href` and `src` in the staged HTML: a relative or site-URL link must reach a file, and a `#id` must exist in its target. Other `https://` links are not followed (no network), `http://` and protocol-relative links fail, and `mailto:`, `roomformac:` and `x-apple.systempreferences:` links are skipped. The staged tree therefore cannot lose a page or an anchor silently (Review Focus 4).
- **Values are checked before they reach markup.** `RFM_REPOSITORY`, `RFM_SITE_URL` and `RFM_FEED_URL` must match strict patterns (no quote, angle bracket, ampersand, backslash or `|`), so a bad configuration value cannot break out of an attribute.
- **Nothing on the site names a payment vendor, and nothing promises what Plan 5 has not built.** The lifetime-licence facts are the spec's (§7.1) without a price; the privacy page says the setup screen's analytics switch only records a choice in this version, because Plan 2 built the switch and Plan 5 has not built the client. Plan 2's seven "What we collect" lines are therefore not copied onto the page yet: nothing is collected, and Plan 5 adds them beside its client.
- **The Open Anyway wording** is the macOS 27 string tables (research §1.3), which agree with Apple's Tahoe guide. Step 3 says "when macOS asks for your login password" rather than fixing the order of the confirmation and the password box: research §2 marks that order as unproven until owner step D4 (a clean-Mac walkthrough).
- **`textSecondary`** is text at 75% in light mode on the site, not the spec's 65%: 65% is 3.8:1 on `canvas`, below WCAG AA for body text (75% is 5.0:1). Dark mode keeps 65% (6.8:1). `grass` and `moss` are only decoration on the site, never text.
- **`download.js` requests only `latest.json`, from the same site.** Every field is validated before it is shown, and the DMG address is never taken from the file: the button's address is fixed in the page and works without JavaScript.


All commands run from the repository root, on the branch `plan6/distribution`, after Tasks 1 and 7 (this task reads what they made). Nothing here builds the app, runs Xcode or reaches the network (Step 9 copies the action pins from Task 13's `release.yml`). The tests never open a browser, a keychain or a system prompt: the page functions run through `osascript -l JavaScript`, which is JavaScriptCore alone.

**Why the checks are shaped this way:**
- The site is static and has no build step, so its tests must read the staged output, which is what ships. `site.bats` stages the real `site/` into a test folder, or stages a copy of what the script reads (a fixture) that a test breaks on purpose. The script finds its root from its own path, so the copy stages the copy.
- The CSS and the two scripts' DOM code cannot be run without a browser. What can be tested is tested: the CSP, the absence of anything external, the exact macOS strings, the colour tokens and both media queries (by text), and the two pure page functions (by execution). Step 11 adds the look, by eye, which no test replaces.
- `workflows.bats` is Task 13's file, so the additions are appended as one block after its last test: no Find text is needed. The block relies only on Task 13's `setup_file` (it skips the whole file without `ruby`, and exports `ROOT` and `WORKFLOWS`, the workflow folder, which `RFM_WORKFLOWS_DIR` can redirect) and defines only helpers whose names start with `pages_`, so it cannot collide with Task 13's `release_` helpers or Task 16's `ci_` ones. It adds no second `setup_file`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing site checks** — `scripts/tests/site.bats`

Bats gotchas that shaped this file, all met before: `run` overwrites the array `$lines`, so no test names a variable `lines`; the `[[ ]]` that is not a test's last statement ends with `|| return 1`; `osascript` and `sed` are called in forms both macOS and Linux accept (`sed -e … -e …`, never `\|` in a basic regex); and the helper `deep_links` skips, instead of failing, on a host without `osascript`.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Checks scripts/stage-site.sh and the pages under site/. The script runs on the
# real site into a test folder, or on a copy of what it reads (a "fixture") that a
# test breaks on purpose. Nothing here needs a browser, the network or a prompt:
# the two page functions run through `osascript -l JavaScript`, which is
# JavaScriptCore alone, with no Apple event.

setup() {
    REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    TMP="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR" && pwd -P)"
    OUT="$TMP/out"
    SCRIPT="$REPO/scripts/stage-site.sh"
    SHA_256="0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
    # shellcheck source=../lib/distribution.sh
    source "$REPO/scripts/lib/distribution.sh"
    REPOSITORY="$(distribution_value "$REPO" RFM_REPOSITORY)"
    SITE_URL="$(distribution_value "$REPO" RFM_SITE_URL)"
    FEED_URL="$(distribution_value "$REPO" RFM_FEED_URL)"
    DMG_URL="https://github.com/$REPOSITORY/releases/latest/download/RoomForMac.dmg"
}

# A copy of what stage-site.sh reads, so a test can break it. The script finds
# its root from its own path, so the copy stages the copy.
make_fixture() {
    FIXTURE="$TMP/fixture"
    mkdir -p "$FIXTURE/scripts/lib" "$FIXTURE/Config"
    cp "$REPO/scripts/stage-site.sh" "$FIXTURE/scripts/"
    cp "$REPO/scripts/lib/distribution.sh" "$FIXTURE/scripts/lib/"
    cp "$REPO/Config/Distribution.xcconfig" "$FIXTURE/Config/"
    cp -R "$REPO/site" "$FIXTURE/site"
}

# A release summary as Task 11's release-summary.sh writes it. $1 is the version.
write_summary() {
    printf '{"schema":1,"version":"%s","build":1000,"minimum_macos":"26.0","date":"2026-09-29","dmg":{"url":"https://github.com/%s/releases/download/v%s/RoomForMac.dmg","size":11840000,"sha256":"%s"}}\n' \
        "$1" "$REPOSITORY" "$1" "$SHA_256" > "$TMP/latest.json"
}

# Stages the real site into $OUT.
stage_real() {
    run "$SCRIPT" "$OUT"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

# Every staged text file the browser would load.
staged_text_files() {
    find "$OUT" -type f \( -name '*.html' -o -name '*.js' -o -name '*.css' \)
}

# Calls roomForMacDeepLink once per argument and prints one line per call:
# the link, or "null". "@undefined" stands for no argument at all.
deep_links() {
    command -v osascript > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "osascript is not available"
    {
        cat "$REPO/site/assets/thanks.js"
        cat << 'JS'
function run(argv) {
    var lines = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
        var result = roomForMacDeepLink(argv[i] === '@undefined' ? undefined : argv[i]);
        lines.push(result === null ? 'null' : result);
    }
    return lines.join('\n');
}
JS
    } > "$TMP/deep-link-driver.js"
    run osascript -l JavaScript "$TMP/deep-link-driver.js" "$@"
}

# Calls roomForMacDownloadDetails once per JSON argument and prints one line per
# call: the details as JSON, or "null".
download_details() {
    command -v osascript > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "osascript is not available"
    {
        cat "$REPO/site/assets/download.js"
        cat << 'JS'
function run(argv) {
    var lines = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
        var summary = null;
        try {
            summary = JSON.parse(argv[i]);
        } catch (error) {
            summary = null;
        }
        var result = roomForMacDownloadDetails(summary);
        lines.push(result === null ? 'null' : JSON.stringify(result));
    }
    return lines.join('\n');
}
JS
    } > "$TMP/download-driver.js"
    run osascript -l JavaScript "$TMP/download-driver.js" "$@"
}

@test "--help prints the usage and exits 0" {
    run "$SCRIPT" --help
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == "Usage: scripts/stage-site.sh <out-dir> [latest.json] [--strict | --strict-from-summary]"* ]] || return 1
    [ ! -e "$OUT" ]
}

@test "bad usage exits 2 and stages nothing" {
    run "$SCRIPT"
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"error: an output folder is required"* ]] || return 1
    run "$SCRIPT" "$OUT" --nope
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"error: unknown argument: --nope"* ]] || return 1
    run "$SCRIPT" "$OUT" latest.json extra.json
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"error: unexpected argument: extra.json"* ]] || return 1
    run "$SCRIPT" "$OUT" --strict-from-summary
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"error: --strict-from-summary needs a latest.json"* ]] || return 1
    [ ! -e "$OUT" ]
}

@test "a folder that has files, or that is inside site/, is refused" {
    mkdir -p "$OUT"
    printf 'keep\n' > "$OUT/keep.txt"
    run "$SCRIPT" "$OUT"
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"is not empty; remove it first"* ]] || return 1
    [ "$(cat "$OUT/keep.txt")" = "keep" ]
    [ "$(ls "$OUT")" = "keep.txt" ]
    run "$SCRIPT" "$REPO/site/staged"
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"error: the output folder must not be inside site/"* ]] || return 1
    [ ! -e "$REPO/site/staged" ]
}

@test "it stages every page, fills every token and inserts the repository and DMG URLs" {
    local page
    stage_real
    for page in index.html open-anyway/index.html thanks/index.html privacy/index.html 404.html \
        assets/site.css assets/download.js assets/thanks.js; do
        [ -s "$OUT/$page" ]

@test "every staged page is locked down by its Content-Security-Policy and loads nothing from elsewhere" {
    local page file tag target
    stage_real
    for page in index.html open-anyway/index.html thanks/index.html privacy/index.html 404.html; do
        # The policy comes before anything the page could load.
        run sed -n -e '/<link/q' -e '/<script/q' -e p "$OUT/$page"
        [[ "$output" == *"<meta http-equiv=\"Content-Security-Policy\" content=\"default-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'\">"* ]] || return 1
        grep -qF '<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">' "$OUT/$page"
        grep -qF '<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">' "$OUT/$page"
        grep -qF '<html lang="en">' "$OUT/$page"
        # A script has a source of its own; no other element carries code or style.
        run grep -o '<script[^>]*>' "$OUT/$page"
        if [ -n "$output" ]; then
            run grep -vc ' src="' <<< "$output"
            [ "$output" = "0" ]
        fi
        run grep -E '<style|<[^>]* (on[a-z]+|style)=' "$OUT/$page"
        [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
        # Scripts, stylesheets and images come from this site, and only from it.
        while IFS= read -r tag; do
            target="${tag#*\"}"
            target="${target%\"}"
            case "$target" in
                http*) [[ "$target" == "$SITE_URL/"* ]] || return 1 ;;
            esac
        done < <(grep -o -E '<(script|img)[^>]* src="[^"]*"|<link[^>]* href="[^"]*"' "$OUT/$page" | grep -o -E '(src|href)="[^"]*"')
    done
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        run grep -nE 'http://|<script src="http|<link href="http|@import|url\(http|url\(//' "$file"
        [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    done < <(staged_text_files)
}

```

`stage_real` stages the real site; `make_fixture` copies the script, `distribution.sh`, `Distribution.xcconfig` and `site/` so a test can break the copy. The helper `deep_links` writes `thanks.js` plus a small `run(argv)` driver to a temporary file and runs it with `osascript -l JavaScript`; `argv` carries the inputs, so an empty string, a newline and `@undefined` (a missing argument) all reach the function. `sed -n -e '/<link/q' -e '/<script/q' -e p` prints a page up to the first thing it could load, which is where the CSP meta must already be.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the failing `pages.yml` checks** — append to `scripts/tests/workflows.bats`

Append this block to the end of the file exactly as it stands: its first line is the blank line that separates it from Task 13's last test, so add no other. It needs no Find text. From the file above it, it uses only `WORKFLOWS`, which Task 13's `setup_file` exports.

```bash

# --- .github/workflows/pages.yml (Task 14) -------------------------------------
# These tests use Task 13's setup_file (it skips the file without ruby, and
# exports WORKFLOWS, the workflow folder) and only the pages_ helpers below, so
# they do not depend on how the release.yml tests above are written. Ruby's YAML
# reads the bare key `on` as the boolean true, so the triggers are read as
# doc["on"] || doc[true].

pages_yml() {
    printf '%s\n' "$WORKFLOWS/pages.yml"
}

# Prints a Ruby expression over the parsed workflow (`doc`, `job` and `on`).
pages_ruby() {
    command -v ruby > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "ruby is not available"
    ruby -ryaml -e '
        doc = YAML.load_file(ARGV[0])
        job = doc["jobs"]["deploy"]
        on = doc["on"] || doc[true]
        puts eval(ARGV[1])
    ' "$(pages_yml)" "$1"
}

@test "pages.yml runs on pushes to the default branches that touch the site, and by hand" {
    run pages_ruby '[on.keys.sort.join(","), on["push"].keys.sort.join(","), on["push"]["branches"].join(","), on["push"]["paths"].join(",")].join("|")'
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = 'push,workflow_dispatch|branches,paths|main,main-mrvlfl|site/**,scripts/stage-site.sh,Config/Distribution.xcconfig' ]
}

@test "pages.yml grants nothing at the top and only what the deploy needs" {
    run pages_ruby 'doc["permissions"].inspect'
    [ "$output" = "{}" ]
    run pages_ruby 'job["permissions"].sort.map { |k, v| "#{k}=#{v}" }.join(",")'
    [ "$output" = "contents=read,id-token=write,pages=write" ]
    run pages_ruby 'doc["defaults"]["run"]["shell"]'
    [ "$output" = "bash" ]
    run pages_ruby 'doc["jobs"].keys.join(",")'
    [ "$output" = "deploy" ]
}

@test "pages.yml deploys only from the default branch, one deployment at a time, to github-pages" {
    run pages_ruby 'job["if"]'
    [ "$output" = "github.ref_name == github.event.repository.default_branch" ]
    run pages_ruby '[job["concurrency"]["group"], job["concurrency"]["cancel-in-progress"]].join(",")'
    [ "$output" = "pages,false" ]
    run pages_ruby '[job["environment"]["name"], job["environment"]["url"]].join(",")'
    [ "$output" = 'github-pages,${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}' ]
    run pages_ruby 'job["runs-on"] + "," + job["timeout-minutes"].to_s'
    [ "$output" = "ubuntu-latest,15" ]
}

@test "pages.yml has the five steps, in order" {
    run pages_ruby 'job["steps"].map { |s| s["name"] }.join("|")'
    [ "$output" = "Check out|Fetch the published summary|Stage the site|Upload the Pages artifact|Deploy" ]
    run pages_ruby 'job["steps"].last["id"]'
    [ "$output" = "deployment" ]
}

@test "pages.yml pins every action by full commit SHA, with its version, on Node 24 majors" {
    run grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:' "$(pages_yml)"
    [ "$output" = "3" ]
    # Every uses: line that is not "owner/repo@<40 hex> # vX.Y.Z" would be counted here.
    run bash -c 'grep -E "^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:" "$1" | grep -vcE "uses: [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+@[0-9a-f]{40} # v[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+$"' _ "$(pages_yml)"
    [ "$output" = "0" ]
    grep -qE 'uses: actions/checkout@[0-9a-f]{40} # v7\.' "$(pages_yml)"
    grep -qE 'uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@[0-9a-f]{40} # v5\.' "$(pages_yml)"
    grep -qE 'uses: actions/deploy-pages@[0-9a-f]{40} # v5\.' "$(pages_yml)"
    # The same commits as release.yml (Task 13), so the two workflows move together:
    # every pin of pages.yml, with its comment, is also a pin of release.yml.
    run bash -c 'grep -oE "uses: [^ ]+ # v[0-9.]+" "$1" | sort -u > "$3/pages.pins"
        grep -oE "uses: [^ ]+ # v[0-9.]+" "$2" | sort -u > "$3/release.pins"
        comm -23 "$3/pages.pins" "$3/release.pins"' _ "$(pages_yml)" "$WORKFLOWS/release.yml" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ]
}

@test "pages.yml stages the site through stage-site.sh and uploads what it staged" {
    run pages_ruby 'job["steps"].find { |s| s["name"] == "Stage the site" }["run"]'
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *'scripts/stage-site.sh build/site "$summary" --strict-from-summary'* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$output" == *"else"$'\n'"    scripts/stage-site.sh build/site"$'\n'"fi"* ]] || return 1
    run pages_ruby 'job["steps"].find { |s| s["name"] == "Upload the Pages artifact" }["with"]["path"]'
    [ "$output" = "build/site" ]
    run pages_ruby 'job["steps"].find { |s| s["name"] == "Fetch the published summary" }["run"]'
    [[ "$output" == *"gh release list --exclude-drafts"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$output" == *'--pattern latest.json'* ]] || return 1
}

@test "pages.yml uses no secret but the workflow's own token, and no pull_request_target" {
    run grep -n 'secrets\.' "$(pages_yml)"
    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    run grep -n 'pull_request_target' "$(pages_yml)"
    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    run grep -c 'github\.token' "$(pages_yml)"
    [ "$output" = "1" ]
    run pages_ruby 'job["steps"].first["with"]["persist-credentials"].inspect'
    [ "$output" = "false" ]
}

@test "pages.yml's run blocks are clean shell" {
    command -v shellcheck > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "shellcheck is not available"
    command -v ruby > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "ruby is not available"
    local count
    count="$(ruby -ryaml -e '
        steps = YAML.load_file(ARGV[0])["jobs"]["deploy"]["steps"]
        runs = steps.map { |s| s["run"] }.compact
        runs.each_with_index { |r, i| File.write(File.join(ARGV[1], "block#{i}.sh"), "#!/bin/bash\n" + r) }
        puts runs.length
    ' "$(pages_yml)" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR")"
    [ "$count" -eq 2 ]
    shellcheck -s bash "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/block0.sh" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/block1.sh"
}
```

`pages_ruby` parses the workflow with Ruby's stdlib YAML (the system Ruby 2.6 on macOS is enough) and evaluates one expression over it; `on` is read as `doc["on"] || doc[true]` because Psych turns a bare `on:` key into `true`. The pin check counts the `uses:` lines that do **not** match `owner/repo@<40 hex> # vX.Y.Z`, so a tag or a branch reference, or a missing version comment, makes the count non-zero; it then requires each of `pages.yml`'s pins to appear, comment included, in `release.yml`. The block reads the workflows through `$WORKFLOWS`, as Task 13's tests do, so `RFM_WORKFLOWS_DIR` points it at a copy too.

On a terminal the summaries read `31 tests, 31 failures` and `8 tests, 8 failures`. (Task 13's own tests are not selected by the filter.) Bats adds a `BW01` warning for each `run` of the missing script (exit code 127, "Command not found"). - [ ] **Step 5: Write `scripts/stage-site.sh`**

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Stage the RoomForMac site for GitHub Pages: copy site/ to a folder, fill in the
# @RFM_…@ tokens from Config/Distribution.xcconfig, and check the result.
#
# Runs on macOS and on ubuntu-latest (release.yml's `pages` job and pages.yml),
# so it uses only bash 3.2 and POSIX tools: no `sed -i`, no `grep -P`, no
# `readlink -f`. Nothing is written to <out-dir> unless every check passed.
#
# Tokens (replaced in *.html and *.js):
#   @RFM_REPOSITORY@  owner/name, from RFM_REPOSITORY
#   @RFM_SITE_URL@    RFM_SITE_URL without a trailing slash
#   @RFM_DMG_URL@     https://github.com/<repository>/releases/latest/download/RoomForMac.dmg
#   @RFM_FEED_URL@    RFM_FEED_URL
# The appcast is never part of the site: it is a release asset (Plan 6, Ruling 3).

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd -P)"
SITE="$ROOT/site"
REQUIRED_FILES="index.html open-anyway/index.html thanks/index.html privacy/index.html 404.html assets/site.css assets/download.js assets/thanks.js"

# shellcheck source=lib/distribution.sh
source "$ROOT/scripts/lib/distribution.sh"

usage() {
    cat << 'EOF'
Usage: scripts/stage-site.sh <out-dir> [latest.json] [--strict | --strict-from-summary]

Copies site/ to <out-dir>, fills in the @RFM_…@ tokens from
Config/Distribution.xcconfig, and copies latest.json when one is given.
Fails on a missing page, a symlink, a token left over, a broken link, or
appcast.xml in site/. <out-dir> must not exist or must be empty.

  --strict               also fail on any "[OWNER:" placeholder (required from v1.0.0)
  --strict-from-summary  --strict when latest.json's version is 1.0.0 or later
                         (needs latest.json; used by pages.yml)

Exit status: 0 staged; 1 a check failed (every problem is printed, and
<out-dir> is left alone); 2 bad usage or a refused <out-dir>.
EOF
}

usage_error() {
    printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    printf 'Run scripts/stage-site.sh --help for usage.\n' >&2
    exit 2
}

failures=0
fail() {
    printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    failures=$((failures + 1))
}

OUT=""
SUMMARY=""
STRICT=0
STRICT_FROM_SUMMARY=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --help | -h)
            usage
            exit 0
            ;;
        --strict) STRICT=1 ;;
        --strict-from-summary) STRICT_FROM_SUMMARY=1 ;;
        -*) usage_error "unknown argument: $1" ;;
        *)
            if [[ -z "$OUT" ]]; then
                OUT="$1"
            elif [[ -z "$SUMMARY" ]]; then
                SUMMARY="$1"
            else
                usage_error "unexpected argument: $1"
            fi
            ;;
    esac
    shift
done
[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || usage_error "an output folder is required"
if [[ "$STRICT_FROM_SUMMARY" -eq 1 && -z "$SUMMARY" ]]; then
    usage_error "--strict-from-summary needs a latest.json"
fi

# The output folder: never inside site/ (checked as written), never a folder that has files.
case "$OUT" in
    /*) out_path="$OUT" ;;
    *) out_path="$PWD/$OUT" ;;
esac
case "$out_path/" in
    "$SITE"/*) usage_error "the output folder must not be inside site/" ;;
esac
if [[ -e "$OUT" ]]; then
    [[ -d "$OUT" ]] || usage_error "$OUT exists and is not a folder"
    if [[ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT")" ]]; then
        usage_error "$OUT is not empty; remove it first"
    fi
fi

# Values the pages get. They end up inside HTML and JavaScript, so each must
# match a strict pattern: no quote, angle bracket, backslash, ampersand or `|`.
repository="$(distribution_value "$ROOT" RFM_REPOSITORY)"
site_url="$(distribution_value "$ROOT" RFM_SITE_URL)"
feed_url="$(distribution_value "$ROOT" RFM_FEED_URL)"
site_url="${site_url%/}"
dmg_url="https://github.com/$repository/releases/latest/download/RoomForMac.dmg"
repository_pattern='^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'
site_pattern='^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$'
feed_pattern='^https://[A-Za-z0-9._~:/?=%+-]+$'
[[ "$repository" =~ $repository_pattern ]] || usage_error "RFM_REPOSITORY must look like owner/name, not '$repository'"
[[ "$site_url" =~ $site_pattern ]] || usage_error "RFM_SITE_URL must be an https URL, not '$site_url'"
[[ "$feed_url" =~ $feed_pattern ]] || usage_error "RFM_FEED_URL must be an https URL, not '$feed_url'"

# The source tree.
[[ -d "$SITE" ]] || usage_error "site/ is missing"
while IFS= read -r link; do
    fail "site/${link#"$SITE"/} is a symlink; Pages refuses symlinks in the artifact"
done < <(find "$SITE" -type l)
for required in $REQUIRED_FILES; do
    if [[ ! -f "$SITE/$required" ]]; then
        fail "missing page or asset: site/$required"
    fi
done
if [[ -e "$SITE/appcast.xml" ]]; then
    fail "site/appcast.xml must not exist: the appcast is a release asset, never part of the site"
fi
if [[ "$failures" -gt 0 ]]; then
    exit 1
fi

TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
TMPDIR="${TMPDIR%/}"
tmp="$(mktemp -d "$TMPDIR/rfm-site.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

cp -R "$SITE"/. "$tmp"/
find "$tmp" -name .DS_Store -type f -exec rm -f {} +

# Fill in the tokens, without `sed -i`.
while IFS= read -r file; do
    LC_ALL=C sed \
        -e "s|@RFM_REPOSITORY@|$repository|g" \
        -e "s|@RFM_SITE_URL@|$site_url|g" \
        -e "s|@RFM_DMG_URL@|$dmg_url|g" \
        -e "s|@RFM_FEED_URL@|$feed_url|g" \
        "$file" > "$file.rfm-tmp"
    mv "$file.rfm-tmp" "$file"
done < <(find "$tmp" -type f \( -name '*.html' -o -name '*.js' \))
while IFS= read -r line; do
    fail "a token is left over in ${line#"$tmp"/}"
done < <(grep -rIn '@RFM_' "$tmp" || true)

# latest.json: the release summary of Task 11, copied as it is once it looks right.
strict="$STRICT"
if [[ -n "$SUMMARY" ]]; then
    if [[ ! -f "$SUMMARY" ]]; then
        fail "latest.json not found: $SUMMARY"
    else
        space='[[:space:]]*'
        grep -Eq "\"schema\"$space:${space}1[,}[:space:]]" "$SUMMARY" || fail "$SUMMARY is not a release summary: schema 1 is missing"
        grep -Eq "\"version\"$space:$space\"[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\"" "$SUMMARY" || fail "$SUMMARY is not a release summary: no X.Y.Z version"
        grep -Eq "\"sha256\"$space:$space\"[0-9a-f]{64}\"" "$SUMMARY" || fail "$SUMMARY is not a release summary: no SHA-256"
        grep -Eq "\"url\"$space:$space\"https://[^\"]+/RoomForMac\\.dmg\"" "$SUMMARY" || fail "$SUMMARY is not a release summary: no RoomForMac.dmg url"
        cp "$SUMMARY" "$tmp/latest.json"
        if [[ "$STRICT_FROM_SUMMARY" -eq 1 ]]; then
            major="$(sed -n "s/.*\"version\"$space:$space\"\\([0-9][0-9]*\\)\\.[0-9][0-9]*\\.[0-9][0-9]*\".*/\\1/p" "$SUMMARY" | head -n 1)"
            if [[ "$major" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$major" -ge 1 ]]; then
                strict=1
            fi
        fi
    fi
fi
if [[ "$strict" -eq 1 ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        fail "--strict: a placeholder is left in ${line#"$tmp"/}"
    done < <(grep -rIn '\[OWNER:' "$tmp" || true)
fi

# Links. Relative links must reach a file (and an id) in the staged tree; links
# built from the site URL are mapped to the tree; other https links are not followed.
# A link that starts with "/" would break under https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/.
normalize() {
    local IFS=/ part result=""
    set -f
    for part in $1; do
        case "$part" in
            "" | .) ;;
            ..)
                if [[ "$result" == */* ]]; then
                    result="${result%/*}"
                elif [[ -n "$result" ]]; then
                    result=""
                else
                    set +f
                    return 1
                fi
                ;;
            *) result="${result:+$result/}$part" ;;
        esac
    done
    set +f
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

check_link() {
    local rel="$1" ref="$2" base="" mapped=0 path fragment target
    case "$ref" in
        "" | mailto:* | tel:* | roomformac:* | x-apple.systempreferences:*) return 0 ;;
        http://*)
            fail "$rel: $ref is not https"
            return 0
            ;;
        //*)
            fail "$rel: $ref is a protocol-relative link"
            return 0
            ;;
        "$site_url" | "$site_url"/* | "$site_url"\?* | "$site_url"\#*)
            ref="${ref#"$site_url"}"
            mapped=1
            ;;
        https://*) return 0 ;;
        /*)
            fail "$rel: $ref starts with '/', which breaks under a project site path"
            return 0
            ;;
        [A-Za-z]*:*)
            fail "$rel: $ref uses a scheme the site does not allow"
            return 0
            ;;
        *)
            base="$(dirname "$rel")"
            if [[ "$base" == "." ]]; then
                base=""
            fi
            ;;
    esac
    fragment=""
    if [[ "$ref" == *"#"* ]]; then
        fragment="${ref#*#}"
    fi
    path="${ref%%#*}"
    path="${path%%\?*}"
    if [[ -z "$path" && "$mapped" -eq 0 ]]; then
        target="$rel" # "#id" or "?query": this page
    else
        case "$path" in
            /*) path="${path#/}" ;;
            *) path="${base:+$base/}$path" ;;
        esac
        if ! target="$(normalize "$path")"; then
            fail "$rel: $ref leaves the site"
            return 0
        fi
        if [[ -z "$target" || -d "$tmp/$target" ]]; then
            target="${target:+$target/}index.html"
        fi
        if [[ ! -f "$tmp/$target" ]]; then
            fail "$rel: broken link $ref"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    if [[ -n "$fragment" ]]; then
        if [[ ! "$fragment" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]]; then
            fail "$rel: $ref has an unusual fragment"
        elif ! grep -q "id=\"$fragment\"" "$tmp/$target"; then
            fail "$rel: $ref points at an id that $target does not have"
        fi
    fi
}

while IFS= read -r page; do
    rel="${page#"$tmp"/}"
    while IFS= read -r ref; do
        check_link "$rel" "$ref"
    done < <(grep -o -E '(href|src)="[^"]*"' "$page" | sed -e 's/^[a-z]*="//' -e 's/"$//' || true)
done < <(find "$tmp" -type f -name '*.html')

if [[ "$failures" -gt 0 ]]; then
    printf 'error: the site was not staged (%d problems)\n' "$failures" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$OUT"
cp -R "$tmp"/. "$OUT"/
count="$(find "$OUT" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
printf 'staged %s files into %s (%s, %s)\n' "$count" "$OUT" "$site_url" "$repository"
```

```bash
chmod +x scripts/stage-site.sh
shellcheck scripts/stage-site.sh
shfmt -d -i 4 -ci -sr scripts/stage-site.sh
```
Expected: no output from any of the three. `shellcheck` follows `# shellcheck source=lib/distribution.sh` through `scripts/.shellcheckrc`, as in CI.

Why it is written this way:
- **Portable to ubuntu-latest.** Only `sed -e`, `grep -E/-o/-r/-I/-n/-q`, `find -type/-name/-exec … {} +`, `cp -R src/. dst/`, `mktemp -d` and `wc` are used, and `LC_ALL=C sed` so a UTF-8 page cannot trip BSD sed. There is no `sed -i` (the replacement writes a `.rfm-tmp` sibling and moves it back), no `grep -P`, no `readlink -f`, no array that can be empty under `set -u` (bash 3.2 rejects `"${empty[@]}"`), and `site.bats` pins that.
- **Every problem in one run.** `fail` prints `error: …` and counts; only after all checks does the script exit 1. Loops that call `fail` read from process substitution, never from a pipe, because a pipe's loop runs in a subshell and would lose the count.
- **Nothing is half-written.** Staging happens in a temporary folder, removed by an `EXIT` trap; `<out-dir>` is created and filled only after the checks pass.
- **The link check** resolves each `href` and `src` by hand: `normalize` collapses `.` and `..` (and refuses a link that climbs out of the site), a folder link resolves to its `index.html`, a `#id` must exist as `id="…"` in the target, and links built from the site URL map back to files. It never resolves a path against the real filesystem outside the staged tree.
- **Strict from the summary.** `--strict-from-summary` reads the major version out of `latest.json` with `sed`, not `jq`, so it also runs where `jq` is missing; the summary is validated first (`schema` 1, a version, a 64-hex SHA-256, a `RoomForMac.dmg` URL), and the copy in the site is the file itself.

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the style sheet** — `site/assets/site.css`

```css
/* RoomForMac site. Alpine Moss tokens from the design spec (§11.1), light and dark.
   No web fonts, no images in CSS, no imports: the pages' Content-Security-Policy is
   default-src 'self'. Mobile first: the base layout is one column that fits 375 px. */

:root {
    color-scheme: light dark;
    --canvas: #F1F0E5;
    --surface: #FCFBF2;
    --text: #333B2D;
    /* The spec's textSecondary is text at 65%, which is 3.8:1 on canvas in light mode.
       The site uses 75% there (5.0:1) so that small text passes WCAG AA. */
    --text-secondary: #62685B;
    --action: #586440;
    --on-action: #FCFBF2;
    --moss: #ADB591;
    --grass: #B3915D;
    --clay: #A8563F;
    --border: rgba(51, 59, 45, 0.16);
    --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(51, 59, 45, 0.08), 0 8px 24px rgba(51, 59, 45, 0.06);
}

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    :root {
        --canvas: #1C2119;
        --surface: #262D22;
        --text: #F1F0E5;
        --text-secondary: #A6A89E;
        --action: #ADB591;
        --on-action: #1C2119;
        --moss: #7E8866;
        --grass: #C9A877;
        --clay: #C97A5F;
        --border: rgba(241, 240, 229, 0.16);
        --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3), 0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25);
    }
}

*,
*::before,
*::after {
    box-sizing: border-box;
}

html {
    -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
    text-size-adjust: 100%;
}

body {
    margin: 0;
    background: var(--canvas);
    color: var(--text);
    font: 1.0625rem/1.55 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", system-ui, sans-serif;
    overflow-wrap: break-word;
}

.wrap {
    width: 100%;
    max-width: 46rem;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 0 16px;
}

.skip {
    position: absolute;
    left: 16px;
    top: -4rem;
    padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
    background: var(--action);
    color: var(--on-action);
    border-radius: 8px;
    z-index: 10;
}

.skip:focus {
    top: 8px;
}

a {
    color: var(--action);
    text-underline-offset: 0.2em;
}

    text-decoration-thickness: 2px;
}

:focus-visible {
    outline: 3px solid var(--action);
    outline-offset: 3px;
    border-radius: 6px;
}

h1,
h2,
h3 {

    margin: 0 0 0.5rem;
    letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}

h1 {
    font-size: 2.25rem;
}

h2 {
    font-size: 1.4rem;
}

h3 {
    font-size: 1.1rem;
}

p,
ul,
ol {
    margin: 0 0 1rem;
}

ul,
ol {
    padding-left: 1.4rem;
}

li {
    margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
}

code {
    font: 0.9em ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace;
    word-break: break-all;
}

.muted {
    color: var(--text-secondary);
}

.small {
    font-size: 0.9375rem;
}

/* Header and footer */

.site-header {
    padding: 16px 0;
}

.site-header .wrap {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;

}

}

/* Hero, buttons, cards */

.hero {

}

.lead {
    font-size: 1.2rem;
    max-width: 34rem;
}

.button {
    display: inline-block;
    padding: 0.8rem 1.5rem;
    background: var(--action);
    color: var(--on-action);
    border-radius: 999px;
    font-weight: 650;
    text-decoration: none;
}

.button:hover {
    filter: brightness(1.08);
}

.button.secondary {
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--action);
    box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--action);
}

.card {
    background: var(--surface);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 20px;
    padding: 1.25rem;
    margin: 1.25rem 0;
    box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}

.card > :last-child {
    margin-bottom: 0;
}

.card.notice {
    border-left: 6px solid var(--moss);
}

details summary {
    cursor: pointer;
    color: var(--action);
}

.facts {
    display: grid;
    gap: 1.25rem;
}

.facts h3 {
    color: var(--action);
}

/* The Open Anyway guide */

.steps {
    list-style: none;
    padding: 0;
    margin: 1.5rem 0;
    counter-reset: step;
}

.step {
    position: relative;
    margin: 0 0 1.5rem;
    padding: 1.25rem 1.25rem 1.25rem 1.25rem;
    background: var(--surface);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 20px;
    box-shadow: var(--shadow);
    counter-increment: step;
}

.step h2::before {
    content: counter(step);
    display: inline-block;
    width: 1.9rem;
    height: 1.9rem;
    margin-right: 0.6rem;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: var(--action);
    color: var(--on-action);
    text-align: center;
    line-height: 1.9rem;
    font-size: 1rem;
}

.step blockquote {
    margin: 0 0 1rem;
    padding: 0 0 0 0.9rem;
    border-left: 3px solid var(--moss);
    color: var(--text-secondary);
}

/* A drawn stand-in for a macOS dialog. It is decorative: the words are in the step. */

.mock {
    margin: 1rem 0 0;
    padding: 1rem;
    max-width: 22rem;
    background: var(--canvas);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 14px;
    font-size: 0.875rem;
    line-height: 1.4;
}

.mock .mock-title {
    margin: 0 0 0.35rem;
    font-weight: 650;
}

.mock .mock-text {
    margin: 0 0 0.9rem;
    color: var(--text-secondary);
}

.mock .mock-row {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 0.6rem;
    margin: 0;
}

.mock .mock-buttons {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    justify-content: flex-end;
    gap: 0.5rem;
    margin: 0;
}

.mock .mock-button {
    display: inline-block;
    padding: 0.3rem 0.9rem;
    background: var(--surface);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 999px;
    font-weight: 600;
}

/* The button to press. The outline is always there; the pulse is added only when
   the reader has not asked for reduced motion. */

.mock .target {
    outline: 3px solid var(--action);
    outline-offset: 2px;
}

@keyframes pulse {
    0% {
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 var(--grass);
    }

    70% {
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 10px transparent;
    }

    100% {
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 transparent;
    }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    .mock .target {
        animation: pulse 1.8s ease-out infinite;
    }
}

/* Wider screens */

@media (min-width: 40rem) {
    h1 {
        font-size: 2.75rem;
    }

    .facts {
        grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
    }

    .card {
        padding: 1.75rem;
    }

    .step {
        padding: 1.5rem 1.75rem;
    }
}

[hidden] {
    display: none !important;
}
```

- Tokens are the spec's §11.1 (light on `:root`, dark under `prefers-color-scheme`), in the CSS custom properties `--canvas`, `--surface`, `--text`, `--action`, `--on-action`, `--moss`, `--grass` and `--clay`. `--text-secondary` is 75% in light mode and the spec's 65% in dark mode (see the decisions above).
- The layout is one column that fits 375 px; only `min-width: 40rem` adds the three-column facts. Nothing has a fixed width, long words break (`overflow-wrap`), and `code` breaks anywhere so the SHA-256 never widens the page.
- The mock dialogs' target keeps its outline always (it is the reduced-motion cue, and also what forced-colors users see); the pulse is a `box-shadow` animation inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and `site.bats` pins that the file has exactly one `animation:` declaration, inside that query.
- No `@import`, no `url()`, no font files: the pages' policy is `default-src 'self'`, and `font-family` names only system fonts.

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the two scripts** — `site/assets/thanks.js`, `site/assets/download.js`

`site/assets/thanks.js`:

```javascript
/* The thanks page: turns "?checkout_id=<id>" into the link that opens RoomForMac.
   Nothing here sends anything anywhere, stores anything or shows the id.

   roomForMacDeepLink is a pure function, so scripts/tests/site.bats runs it with
   osascript -l JavaScript. Its rules mirror RoomForMac/App/DeepLink.swift
   (DeepLink.parse): exactly one parameter, named checkout_id, whose value is 1 to
   128 ASCII letters, digits, "_" or "-". A page rule can only be stricter than the
   app's: this function never decodes "%" escapes, so it refuses what the app would
   decode. The constants below are checked against DeepLink.swift by site.bats. */

var ROOMFORMAC_LINK_SCHEME = 'roomformac';
var ROOMFORMAC_LINK_HOST = 'purchased';
var ROOMFORMAC_LINK_PARAMETER = 'checkout_id';
var ROOMFORMAC_CHECKOUT_ID_MAX = 128;

// "?checkout_id=<id>" -> "roomformac://purchased?checkout_id=<id>", or null.
function roomForMacDeepLink(search) {
    if (typeof search !== 'string' || search.charAt(0) !== '?') {
        return null;
    }
    var pairs = search.slice(1).split('&');
    if (pairs.length !== 1) {
        return null;
    }
    var prefix = ROOMFORMAC_LINK_PARAMETER + '=';
    if (pairs[0].indexOf(prefix) !== 0) {
        return null;
    }
    var id = pairs[0].slice(prefix.length);
    if (id.length < 1 || id.length > ROOMFORMAC_CHECKOUT_ID_MAX) {
        return null;
    }
    if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(id)) {
        return null;
    }
    return ROOMFORMAC_LINK_SCHEME + '://' + ROOMFORMAC_LINK_HOST + '?' + prefix + id;
}

(function () {
    if (typeof document === 'undefined') {
        return; // Not a browser: the tests load this file to call the function above.
    }
    var link = roomForMacDeepLink(window.location.search);
    var button = document.getElementById('open-app');
    var opening = document.getElementById('open-status');
    var unreadable = document.getElementById('link-unreadable');
    if (link === null) {
        if (unreadable !== null) {
            unreadable.hidden = false;
        }
        return;
    }
    if (button !== null) {
        button.setAttribute('href', link);
        button.hidden = false;
    }
    if (opening !== null) {
        opening.hidden = false;
    }
    // One attempt. Chrome ignores a custom-scheme launch that has no user gesture,
    // and no browser says whether an app answered, so the button stays as well.
    window.setTimeout(function () {
        window.location.href = link;
    }, 600);
})();
```

`roomForMacDeepLink` mirrors `DeepLink.parse` rule by rule and is only ever stricter: it needs the leading `?`, exactly one pair named `checkout_id`, and 1 to 128 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, and it never decodes `%` escapes (the app would decode `%41` to `A`; the page refuses it, which is safe because the page's output is always something the app accepts). The four `ROOMFORMAC_…` constants are compared with `DeepLink.swift` by `site.bats`, so a Plan 5 change to the parameter name or the length limit fails there until both files agree. The anonymous function at the bottom returns at once when there is no `document`, which is how `osascript` loads the file. Its one navigation is the timeout that runs once, after 600 ms; `hidden` (not inline styles, which the CSP forbids) shows and hides the parts of the page.

`site/assets/download.js`:

```javascript
/* The download page: shows the version, size and SHA-256 of the current release.
   The Download button does not need this file: its address is fixed in the page.
   The only request is for latest.json on this same site, which release.yml and
   pages.yml stage from the release summary. Nothing is stored, and nothing is sent
   apart from that request. */

// A release summary (schema 1, Task 11) -> { version, megabytes, sha256 }, or null
// when it is not one. Every field is checked, because the page shows them.
function roomForMacDownloadDetails(summary) {
    if (summary === null || typeof summary !== 'object' || summary.schema !== 1) {
        return null;
    }
    var dmg = summary.dmg;
    if (dmg === null || typeof dmg !== 'object') {
        return null;
    }
    if (typeof summary.version !== 'string' || !/^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/.test(summary.version)) {
        return null;
    }
    if (typeof dmg.size !== 'number' || !isFinite(dmg.size) || dmg.size <= 0 || Math.floor(dmg.size) !== dmg.size) {
        return null;
    }
    if (typeof dmg.sha256 !== 'string' || !/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(dmg.sha256)) {
        return null;
    }
    return {
        version: summary.version,
        megabytes: (dmg.size / 1000000).toFixed(1),
        sha256: dmg.sha256
    };
}

(function () {
    if (typeof document === 'undefined' || typeof window.fetch !== 'function') {
        return; // Not a browser: the tests load this file to call the function above.
    }
    var details = document.getElementById('download-details');
    var version = document.getElementById('download-version');
    var checksum = document.getElementById('download-sha256');
    if (details === null || version === null || checksum === null) {
        return;
    }
    window.fetch('latest.json', { cache: 'no-cache' })
        .then(function (response) {
            return response.ok ? response.json() : null;
        })
        .then(function (summary) {
            var info = roomForMacDownloadDetails(summary);
            if (info === null) {
                return;
            }
            version.textContent = 'Version ' + info.version + ' · ' + info.megabytes + ' MB';
            checksum.textContent = info.sha256;
            details.hidden = false;
        })
        .catch(function () {
            // No summary yet, or offline: the button alone is enough.
        });
})();
```

`roomForMacDownloadDetails` accepts only a complete schema-1 summary and returns three plain strings, which the page puts in with `textContent`; the address of the DMG is not read from the file. The one request is `fetch('latest.json', …)` on the same site, and `site.bats` pins that it is the only `fetch(` in the site's scripts.

```html
<div class="wrap">
<h1>Open RoomForMac the first time</h1>
<p class="lead">macOS blocks apps that Apple has not notarized. RoomForMac is one of them. Approve it once in System Settings, in three steps, and it opens with a double-click from then on.</p>

<ol class="steps">
<li class="step">
<h2>Try to open it</h2>
<p>Open RoomForMac from your Applications folder. If you are still in the disk image, drag RoomForMac to Applications first. macOS shows this message:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>“RoomForMac” Not Opened</p>
<p>Apple could not verify “RoomForMac” is free of malware that may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Click <strong>Done</strong>. Do not click Move to Trash.</p>
<figure class="mock" role="img" aria-label="Drawing of the macOS message “RoomForMac” Not Opened, with the Done button highlighted.">
<p class="mock-title" aria-hidden="true">“RoomForMac” Not Opened</p>
<p class="mock-text" aria-hidden="true">Apple could not verify “RoomForMac” is free of malware that may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy.</p>
<p class="mock-buttons" aria-hidden="true"><span class="mock-button">Move to Trash</span><span class="mock-button target">Done</span></p>
</figure>
</li>

<li class="step">
<h2>Open Privacy &amp; Security</h2>
<p>Choose Apple menu, then System Settings. Click <strong>Privacy &amp; Security</strong> in the sidebar and scroll down to <strong>Security</strong>. Next to this line, click <strong>Open Anyway</strong>:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>“RoomForMac” was blocked to protect your Mac.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>The button is there for about an hour after step 1. If it is gone, do step 1 again.</p>
<p><a class="button secondary" href="x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.settings.PrivacySecurity.extension?Security">Open Privacy &amp; Security</a></p>
<p class="muted small">Or by hand: Apple menu → System Settings → Privacy &amp; Security → Security.</p>
<figure class="mock" role="img" aria-label="Drawing of System Settings, Privacy &amp; Security, Security: “RoomForMac” was blocked to protect your Mac, with the Open Anyway button highlighted.">
<p class="mock-row" aria-hidden="true"><span>“RoomForMac” was blocked to protect your Mac.</span><span class="mock-button target">Open Anyway</span></p>
</figure>
</li>

<li class="step">
<h2>Confirm</h2>
<p>macOS asks you once more:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Open “RoomForMac”?</p>
<p>Apple is not able to verify that it is free from malware that could harm your Mac or compromise your privacy. Don’t open this unless you are certain it is from a trustworthy source.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Click <strong>Open Anyway</strong>. When macOS asks for your login password, or for Touch ID, give it and click <strong>OK</strong>. The password box is macOS’s own. It reads:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Privacy &amp; Security</p>
<p>You are attempting to open an app that may cause harm to your Mac or compromise your privacy</p>
</blockquote>
<p>RoomForMac opens. From now on, open it like any other app.</p>
<figure class="mock" role="img" aria-label="Drawing of the macOS question Open “RoomForMac”? with the Open Anyway button highlighted.">
<p class="mock-title" aria-hidden="true">Open “RoomForMac”?</p>
<p class="mock-text" aria-hidden="true">Apple is not able to verify that it is free from malware that could harm your Mac or compromise your privacy. Don’t open this unless you are certain it is from a trustworthy source.</p>
<p class="mock-buttons" aria-hidden="true"><span class="mock-button">Cancel</span><span class="mock-button target">Open Anyway</span></p>
</figure>
</li>
</ol>
<p class="muted small">The drawings only show where to click. Your Mac’s windows may look a little different. Apple’s own instructions: <a href="https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mh40616/26/mac/26">Open a Mac app from an unknown developer</a> and <a href="https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445">Safely open apps on your Mac</a>.</p>

<section class="card" aria-labelledby="safe">
<h2 id="safe">Is this safe?</h2>
<p>Open Anyway is Apple’s own way to approve an app that is not notarized. It makes an exception for this one app and nothing else.</p>
<p>RoomForMac is open source, so anyone can read what it does: it is on <a href="https://github.com/@RFM_REPOSITORY@">GitHub</a>. Every release lists the SHA-256 checksum of its download. Approve only a copy you downloaded from this site or from the project’s <a href="https://github.com/@RFM_REPOSITORY@/releases/latest">release page</a>.</p>
<p>RoomForMac is signed with its own certificate, not an Apple one. macOS uses that signature to recognise the app after an update, so the permissions you gave it stay in place.</p>
</section>

<section class="card notice" aria-labelledby="terminal">
<h2 id="terminal">We never ask you to paste commands into Terminal</h2>
<p>The three steps above use System Settings only. If a web page, a video or a message tells you to run a command to open RoomForMac, do not: it did not come from us.</p>
</section>

<section aria-labelledby="trouble">
<h2 id="trouble">If something goes wrong</h2>
<h3>There is no Open Anyway button</h3>
<p>The button appears only after macOS has blocked the app, and it stays for about an hour. Do step 1 again, then go straight to step 2.</p>
<h3>“RoomForMac” is damaged and can’t be opened.</h3>
<p>The download is incomplete or was changed on the way. Delete it and <a href="../">download RoomForMac again</a>.</p>
<h3>It opens from the disk image, but it can’t update</h3>
<p>RoomForMac has to live in your Applications folder to update itself. Drag it from the disk image to Applications, eject the disk image, and open the copy in Applications.</p>
<h3>Still stuck?</h3>
<p>Tell us what macOS showed you, on <a href="https://github.com/@RFM_REPOSITORY@/issues">GitHub</a>.</p>
</section>
</div>
```
